text:
amir: Proposal: move default SIEM export retention for transient operational indices from 90d -> 30d. Create a quarantined 'forensic snapshots' flow for any evidence we need to preserve. Thoughts on RBAC and KMS gating?

laura: which indices are you marking as transient? please enumerate so we don't accidentally include auth/audit.

amir: shortlist: edge-requests, worker-heartbeats, infra-metrics, ci-build-output (no user payload). Excludes: auth-events, user-audit, iam-logs.

sophie: we should add a mandatory PII-scrub step before any export can be snapshotted. Regex-based scrub + tokenization for emails/phones.

kevin: agree. Also recommend all snapshots go into a separate S3 bucket with server-side KMS encryption (separate key) and lifecycle policy. That makes enforcement simpler.

sec-automation: Note: Snapshot writes must include metadata {ticket, requester, reason}. Audit events to secure-ops-audit (retention 730d).

laura: RBAC idea: no one can read raw snapshots by default. Flow: request -> OPA policy check -> manager approval -> KMS-proxy mints ephemeral decrypt token (TTL 1h) -> consumer uses token. Only sec-analyst role can request.

amir: I'd like the token issuance to be a service call rather than handing out keys. Example: POST /kms-proxy/unwrap?ticket=INC-456 returns bearer token scoped to snapshot ID.

kevin: implement service that logs to secure-ops-audit and writes a signed S3 presigned URL with short TTL. That way ops never keep keys.

sophie: For incident response, allow an "evidence-hold" tag that prevents lifecycle deletion. To enable it requires 2 approvers (sec-lead + legal).

legal: If the snapshot is potentially PII or breach evidence, our team must be notified and review before extension. Two approvers is fine, but include timezone SLA for approval (e.g., 4 hours).

amir: cost estimate: current 90d -> 30d on transient indices saves approx $1.8k/month in hot SIEM storage for prod region (rough). Keeping sealed evidence under hold will add negligible cost.

sec-automation: detection rule: alert when unwrap_count(snapshot_id) > 2 in 24h OR unwraps_by_different_principals > 1. Send to #incidents and create incident if threshold hit.

kevin: terraform snippet for bucket policy we can use (pseudo):
resource "aws_s3_bucket" "forensic" {
  bucket = "redwood-forensics-${var.env}"
  server_side_encryption_configuration {
    rule {
      apply_server_side_encryption_by_default {
        sse_algorithm = "aws:kms"
        kms_master_key_id = var.forensic_kms_key
      }
    }
  }
}
add lifecycle rule: expire after 30 days unless tag "evidence-hold" = "true"

laura: also require object-level tagging and an S3 bucket policy that denies GetObject unless request contains X-Amz-Security-Token matching our ephemeral tokens.

kevin: OPA policy example (short): allow if requester in sec-analyst AND ticket_valid AND manager_approved. We'll embed in the proxy.

amir: tabletop: Let's run a 1-hour drill next week: request a snapshot, approve, unwrap, detect abnormal unwrap pattern. We'll time the approvals.

sophie: I'll draft the PII-scrub pipeline: redaction rules, replace with token placeholders, and add a checksum so decrypted snapshot integrity is verifiable.

legal: add a checklist in the runbook for escalation to legal when evidence-hold is requested. Also include retention justification for regulators.

devops-bot: Reminder: update /docs/oncall and /docs/forensics within 72h of policy approval.

amir: Action items:
- Sophie: PII-scrub pipeline draft (ETA 3d)
- Kevin: KMS-proxy + bucket policy PR (ETA 5d)
- Laura: OPA policy & IAM role snippets (ETA 2d)
- Legal: evidence-hold playbook and approval SLA (ETA 4d)
- Sec-automation: detection rules and alerts (ETA 2d)

kevin: I'll prototype the proxy today and post endpoints.

amir: thanks. We'll collect PRs and lock the retention change once we validate the PII-scrub and proxy in staging.
